Magnitude difference between the frequency and probability views

Source: R/magnitude_difference.R
magnitude_difference.Rd

magnitude_difference() measures, edge by edge, how far the two usual summaries of one set of sequences disagree: the raw transition counts (frequency network, FTNA, build_network(method = "frequency")) and the row-conditional probabilities (TNA, build_network(method = "relative")). It builds both networks from the same event log or wide sequences, puts the two weight matrices on a common scale and returns the per-edge discrepancy, the magnitude difference, under one of five metrics.

The two matrices rank edges differently because row normalisation divides each count by its source state's total: an edge that is large in counts can be modest in probability when its source state is frequent, and an edge from a rare source state can dominate its row in probability. A large magnitude difference marks an edge whose importance depends on which view is reported; it says nothing about sampling uncertainty, which bootstrap_network() estimates for each view.

Usage

magnitude_difference(
  data,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  metric = c("abs_diff", "chord_dist", "atanh_diff", "geom_norm_diff", "cv_inflation"),
  scale = c("tna_range", "rank_minmax", "minmax", "none"),
  format = c("auto", "long", "wide")
)

# S3 method for class 'magnitude_difference'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'magnitude_difference'
plot(x, type = c("stacked", "circular"), min_show = 0.01, title = NULL, ...)

Arguments

data

The event log (long format, with action set) or wide sequences, as a data frame.

actor, action, time

The columns of a long event log, as in build_network(). Column names are not read: without action the data is read as wide sequences, and a frame whose roles cannot be told raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, as does a name that is not a column of data. Default NULL.

metric

The discrepancy metric, computed on the two scaled weight vectors. "abs_diff" (default) is the absolute difference; "chord_dist" the absolute difference after each vector is scaled to unit length (chord distance on the unit sphere); "atanh_diff" the absolute difference of the Fisher z (atanh()) transforms, with values capped at 1 - 1e-6, so it needs weights in [0, 1) and is not meaningful with scale = "none"; "geom_norm_diff" the absolute difference after each vector is divided by its geometric mean (of the weights plus 0.001, so zeros are allowed), which enlarges small edges; and "cv_inflation" the absolute difference after each vector is divided by its standard deviation (at least 0.001).

scale

How the two weight matrices are put on a common scale before differencing. "tna_range" (default) rescales the counts linearly into the [min, max] range of the probabilities and leaves the probabilities as they are, so the difference is in probability units. "rank_minmax" replaces each matrix's values by their ranks scaled to [0, 1] (ordinal). "minmax" scales each matrix to [0, 1] separately, so the two maxima map to the same value although their native ranges differ. "none" uses the raw weights.

format

The input format passed to build_network(). "auto" (default) reads wide sequences when action is NULL and an event log otherwise; "long" and "wide" force a reading.

x

For the print() and plot() methods: a magnitude_difference object.

...

For the plot() method: further settings of the drawing. "stacked" takes threshold (the magnitude marked "small" in the colour key, default 10% of the largest), r_inner, r_outer, gap_rad, label_offset, label_size and src_label_size; "circular" takes self_loops (default TRUE), label_offset and edge_curve. The print() method ignores it.

type

For the plot() method: the kind of plot. "stacked" (default) is a polar portrait with one sector per source state and one wedge per edge, grey up to the smaller of the two scaled weights and coloured by the magnitude difference from there to the larger; edges absent from both views are left out. "circular" is a chord-style diagram of the signed difference (tna - ftna), its colour giving the sign and its width and opacity the magnitude.

min_show

For type = "circular": edges whose magnitude difference is below this fraction of the largest are left out. Default 0.01.

title

For the plot() method: the plot title. Default NULL, which names the metric and the scale.

Value

A magnitude_difference object. print() reports the metric, the scale, the states, the number of edges and the minimum, quartiles, mean and maximum of the magnitude differences; plot() draws them. The object's fields:

edges

One row per ordered pair of states (the self-transitions and absent edges included), with the columns from, to, ftna and tna (the scaled weights), signed (tna - ftna) and value (the chosen metric).

metric, scale

The metric and scale used.

weights_ftna, weights_tna

The two scaled weight matrices.

states

The state names.

For the plot() method: a ggplot object. The print() method returns x invisibly.

See also

build_network(), compare_model()

Examples

data(group_regulation_long, package = "Nestimate")
fit <- magnitude_difference(group_regulation_long,
                            actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
                            time = "Time")
print(fit)
#> magnitude_difference object
#>   metric: abs_diff   scale: tna_range 
#>   states (9):  adapt, cohesion, consensus, coregulate, discuss, emotion, monitor, plan, synthesis
#>   edges: 81 
#>   magnitude-difference summary (abs_diff):
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> 0.00000 0.01143 0.03002 0.06035 0.06894 0.42910 
# \donttest{
# The polar portrait shows which edges row-normalization promotes.
plot(fit)                       # stacked polar portrait

plot(fit, type = "circular")    # chord-style diagram

# }
